- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when recent history shows upward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 75+), often overshooting by 2–5% and failing to reflect mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Underreacts to downward price corrections; often fails to adjust forecast downward when true outcome shows a clear decline.
- Overestimates volatility in the first 5–7 days of forecast, then gradually converges toward true mean, suggesting a “warm-up” bias.
- When history includes a recent low, model often fails to recognize it as a bottom and continues to forecast upward.
- Forecast mean is typically 1–3% below true outcome, especially in the first 10 days — adjust upward by 1–2% for early periods.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends beyond 3–5 days; true price often reverts to 1–2 standard deviations below recent peak after spikes.
